headline: Medium risk: Airflow can feed dbt with unverified outputs, creating default-path cascading errors and moderate data-leakage exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can move content through files/APIs and dbt consumes warehouse inputs, so a manual or pipeline bridge could carry malicious instructions. However, neither profile shows a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP channel, and no direct parser-permissiveness evidence is present. The interaction is plausible but not documented, so I choose low rather than none due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF Airflow writes attacker-controlled text into a file or API payload that dbt later parses as instructions
IF an operator manually copies Airflow output into dbt configuration or macros
mitigations: Restrict Airflow outputs to structured data only
Add a manual review step before dbt consumes upstream text
Use separate workspaces for orchestration and modeling
Sanitize any templated SQL or YAML inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between Airflow and dbt

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress and dbt touches data warehouse data, so a shared pipeline can move sensitive warehouse content through Airflow outputs into dbt processing. The profiles do not show explicit secrets handling or a shared OS workspace, but the default data-engineering workflow still creates a realistic leakage path. Uncertainty about exact deployment should not lower the severity.
conditions: IF Airflow tasks read warehouse rows and emit them into logs, XCom, or downstream files
IF dbt runs against the same warehouse objects that Airflow exports
mitigations: Mask sensitive columns before Airflow emits them
Disable verbose task logging for data-bearing steps
Separate staging and production warehouse credentials
Review dbt models for unintended column propagation
requires-engineering: enforce row/column-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents are data-engineering tools, but the profiles do not show overlapping write permissions to the same filesystem, git state, or database. Airflow has broad egress and dbt has allowlisted egress, yet neither profile requests elevated privileges or shared mutable-resource scopes. The conflict pathway is possible only if an operator wires them to the same writable target, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory or database objects
IF an orchestrator grants both write access to the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts
Split staging and modeling write targets
Lock shared tables during writes
Use per-agent output directories
requires-engineering: add concurrency locks around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can generate upstream pipeline outputs and dbt can consume warehouse inputs, so dbt may treat Airflow-produced artifacts as authoritative without an explicit verification step. The profiles do not document validation between them, and no evidence shows dbt critically evaluating Airflow outputs by default. That makes a default-path cascading error plausible and more than low severity.
conditions: IF dbt models are built from Airflow-produced intermediate tables or files
IF no validation step checks schema, freshness, or row counts before dbt runs
mitigations: Add schema checks before dbt execution
Compare row counts between upstream and downstream stages
Require freshness assertions on Airflow outputs
Quarantine new upstream datasets before promotion
requires-engineering: implement automated data-quality gates

E_compliance.rationale: Airflow is documented as a general orchestrator with broad egress, while dbt touches data warehouse data. If warehouse data includes regulated or residency-bound records, the pair can move that data through different retention or jurisdictional controls. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR status, so I cannot raise higher, but the compliance mismatch remains plausible in default analytics deployments.
conditions: IF the warehouse contains regulated or residency-bound records
IF Airflow logs, exports, or retries persist those records outside the warehouse policy
mitigations: Classify warehouse datasets before orchestration
Redact regulated fields from logs
Align retention settings across both tools
Restrict Airflow to approved regions
requires-engineering: add policy checks for residency and retention
